subject: Post-demo: Cloudima cost deep-dive & proposed test matrix
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@cloudima.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Cloudima cost deep-dive & proposed test matrix

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and where we think to go next so we keep momentum:  

What we covered:  
- High-level cost delta: based on the demo prompts we ran, Redwood median effective unit cost (prompt+completion) modelled at ~ $11.8 / 1M tokens versus the hyperscaler benchmark you referenced (approx. $17–19 / 1M tokens for the same model family and quantization). These are conservative: assume 30% cache hit, batching size ~4.
- Differentiators we called out: predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated), continuous prefix/KV caching (replay-friendly for chat), and router-based fallbacks to lower-cost quantized variants when latency SLOs allow.
- Risk areas you highlighted: tokenization parity, measuring completion vs total tokens, and how cache hit rates translate to real-world savings.

Proposed immediate objective: a focused cost delta test that answers 1) per-1M token delta under realistic user patterns, 2) sensitivity to batching, and 3) impact of cache hit-rate assumptions (cold vs warm).

Action items (proposed):
1) Redwood provides a reproducible test matrix + sample harness (we attach a starter spreadsheet and one-pager).
2) Cloudima runs two canary windows (production-like traffic for 24h each) — we characterize cold-start and warm-cache runs.
3) Redwood runs an isolated micro-benchmark for batching sizes {1,4,8,16} and reports tokens/sec and p99 latency for the same model config.
4) Both sides agree the tokenization policy (GPT-style byte-pair) and whether system prompts are to be included in the "per-1M" measurement.

If that looks good I can loop in SE (Ben) for the test matrix and ops runbook, and we can get a short PoC SOW signed (we can use the attached doc + DocuSign link).

Attachments: redwood-cloudima-one-pager.pdf, cloudima-cost-model-v1.xlsx

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
From: Priya Sharma <priya@cloudima.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cicorp.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T17:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Cloudima cost deep-dive & proposed test matrix

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we lock things in:  

1) Tokenization: we want to confirm that your "per-1M" includes system prompts + user query + model completion. Our billing team counts everything inside the API call; if you exclude system prompts that will bias the comparison.
2) Cache: are you modeling prefix cache (conversation-level reuse) or user-keyed KV cache? For our product, prefix reuse (shared warm prefixes across users) is the main source of savings.
3) Benchmarks: can you provide the exact model variant names (and quantization) you used for the demo numbers? Our procurement will ask for exact references.

Also, include your legal/procurement contact — we'll need a PoC SOW and an initial procurement checklist for internal approval. I'm CC'ing Tom (procurement) since he'll handle the SOW.

Priya
Priya Sharma
Director of AI Platform, Cloudima
priya@cloudima.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@cloudima.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Cloudima cost deep-dive & proposed test matrix

Hi Priya — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and a proposed test matrix (attachments).

1) Per-1M token definition: we measure total tokens sent to the model (system + user + assistant). Our spreadsheets and the attached cost model use that convention. We'll include a per-component breakdown in the benchmark output so you can filter out system tokens if needed.

2) Cache type: Redwood's KV/prefix cache supports both (a) conversation-prefix caching (shared prefix blocks) and (b) user-keyed KV entries. For the savings we quoted we assumed prefix caching with a 30% hit rate (shared across similar queries). We'll model user-keyed separately in the test matrix.

3) Model details used in demo: redwood-7b-q4f16 (quantized variant) and redwood-13b-raw for baseline comparisons. For hyperscaler comparisons we matched architecture closest-available endpoints (we list the exact endpoint IDs in the Drive link).

Proposed test matrix (high level):
- Micro-benchmarks (Redwood hosted): batching sizes = [1,4,8,16], sequence lengths = [128,512,1024], 1000 runs each. Measure tokens/sec, cost per-1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency.
- Cache scenarios: cold (0% hit), warm-shared (30% hit), hot (60%+ hit). For each, measure effective token reduction, cache lookup latency added, and any increase in tail latency.
- End-to-end canary: run two 24h windows against your sandbox traffic generator; we will instrument and produce per-route cost/latency breakdowns.

I've attached test-matrix.csv and a sample runner command we use internally. Will also upload the raw harness to the shared Drive.

Attachments: test-matrix.csv

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Tom/Priya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Concrete next steps and timeline below:  

1) Redwood will upload a PoC SOW template by EOD (DocuSign link included). Goal: signed within 72 hours.
2) Ben will provision the micro-benchmark harness and Drive folder today (links in related_links).
3) Redwood provides a conservative spend estimate for the two 24h canaries: 
   - Cold run (0% cache): est. 1.2M tokens -> ~$14.50 (Redwood hosted estimate using redwood-7b-q4f16) *per-1M basis; total ~$17.40 for the run.
   - Warm run (30% hit assumed): est. effective tokens 0.84M -> proportional cost ~$9.95.
   (These are illustrative; Ben's micro-benchmarks will produce final per-1M numbers and p99 tails.)
4) Schedule: canary kickoff proposed Wed 2027-09-29; preliminary results delivered by close of day Thu 2027-09-30.

Priya/Tom — if that timeline works, I'll put the SOW and HubSpot milestone into place and we can move forward.
